decisions.justification: Q1 explicitly asked what should happen when a target already exists, and the user chose refusal of the whole run with no overwrite or skipping.
Q5 explicitly asked whether runtime failures must roll back completed renames, and the user answered yes.
Q8 asked whether source-to-self mappings should be harmless no-ops, and the user agreed they should not be executed.
Q2 explicitly asked whether a target vacated by another planned rename should be allowed, and the user accepted chains and swaps.
The agent never asked what a second identical run should do, despite README.md documenting frequent accidental repeat runs.
No question addressed case-only renames or collision semantics on case-insensitive filesystems.
Q4, Q6, Q7, and Q10 asked about report contents, streams, exit status, and rollback-failure details.
The session never settled whether preview or confirmation should be part of the fix or whether safety could depend on it.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: a run that cannot complete leaves every file unchanged

notes: The session thoroughly specified collision handling, transaction rollback, and failure reporting, and the implementation visibly reflects those choices. It over-questioned implementation details without first declaring the expected bounded path, added a redundant final approval gate, and missed explicit treatment of repeat-run idempotency, case-insensitive filesystems, and preview policy. The check-then-rename sequence can still overwrite a target that appears between those operations on filesystems where rename replaces an existing destination, so the absolute no-overwrite requirement is not fully met.
